stimulus: Transcript: "Can I keep the laptop overnight? We wipe and reinstall everything on it."
question: Which is the most natural reply?

options.A: Overnight's fine, my roommate has a spare.
options.B: Go ahead, everything important is on there anyway.
options.C: Sure, I'll pick it up first thing tomorrow morning.
options.D: That's fine, once I've copied my files off the desktop.

stimulus: Transcript: "Grey, library sticker on the front — that's what you told my colleague?"
question: Which is the most natural reply?

options.A: That's the one, grey with the sticker on the front.
options.B: I told him grey, so someone wrote it down wrong.
options.C: Right, I filled that form in with him yesterday.
options.D: Could you check the back room as well?

stimulus: Transcript: "I clock out at nine — want me to wait while you eat?"
question: Which is the most natural reply?

options.A: Go ahead and clock out, I'll box mine up.
options.B: What time does the grill open in the morning?
options.C: Stay if you don't mind, I've barely started this.
options.D: Nine's earlier than I thought you shut.

stimulus: Transcript: "Is there another copy? The access code in this one's been used."
question: Which is the most natural reply?

options.A: I can knock the price down if you want to keep it.
options.B: Yeah, the codes are usually gone on the used ones.
options.C: You can buy the code by itself online.
options.D: I'll swap it for a new one from the back.

stimulus: Transcript: "Want to wait on the key till the third form's in?"
question: Which is the most natural reply?

options.A: Sure, hold it until everything's in.
options.B: Which one are you still waiting on?
options.C: I can pick it up any afternoon this week.
options.D: How late is the office open for key pickup?

stimulus: Transcript: "Your treadmill by the window keeps cutting out."
question: Which is the most natural reply?

options.A: The mirror row's free right now if you'd rather move.
options.B: That whole row was serviced last week, so it should be fine.
options.C: They all cut out when the belt warms up; that one's old.
options.D: I'll swap the safety key on it — two minutes, tops.

stimulus: Transcript: "They go every half hour, forty minutes — 4:40 makes your five?"
question: Which is the most natural reply?

options.A: Five-ten would be fine if that class ever started on time.
options.B: Better put me on the 4:10 then, I can't turn up late.
options.C: 4:40 works, I'll be at the stop by half past.
options.D: Is the 4:40 the one that stops at the library?

stimulus: Transcript: "Can I renew this until the twentieth? My presentation's on the twenty-second."
question: Which is the most natural reply?

options.A: Is this checked out under your name or a department account?
options.B: Let's make it the twenty-third, so you've still got it that morning.
options.C: Good luck with it. Is the presentation for a class or a seminar?
options.D: Sure, the twentieth works. It'll be due back at six that evening, then.

stimulus: Transcript: "Could you add my name to the slides Priya's had since Monday?"
question: Which is the most natural reply?

options.A: Priya's the one with the file — you'd have to ask her.
options.B: Sam handles the title slide, I think — try him first.
options.C: You were listed on Monday's version already, I'm pretty sure.
options.D: Sure, I'll put your name on the deck tonight.

stimulus: Transcript: "So it's one more semester of coursework, then applications in the fall."
question: Which is the most natural reply?

options.A: I know it's taken me a while. I'll try to move quicker.
options.B: Would that be the fall deadlines or the spring ones?
options.C: That's right, one more semester and then the applications go out.
options.D: If you think that's the smarter route, I'll plan around that.

stimulus: Transcript: "So that's twelve hours for you this week — two fives and a four?"
question: Which is the most natural reply?

options.A: Could you make it two sixes next week?
options.B: That comes to fourteen, not twelve.
options.C: I picked up one of those shifts from Dana.
options.D: Twelve sounds right, thanks for checking.

stimulus: Transcript: "Can you email me that draft before I leave for Denver?"
question: Which is the most natural reply?

options.A: Sure, I'll email it Sunday night after I finish the last section.
options.B: I'll send it over sometime next week, once the data's cleaned up.
options.C: When are you flying out? I'd rather not cut it close.
options.D: Denver's supposed to be freezing. How long are you out there?

stimulus: Transcript: "It's ten-fifty now. Any chance someone could see me before eleven?"
question: Which is the most natural reply?

options.A: Ten minutes isn't enough for a visit, I'm afraid.
options.B: Have you been seen here before, or is this your first visit?
options.C: Take a seat, someone will be with you shortly.
options.D: I can't move you ahead of the people already waiting, sorry.

options.B: Tonight works — I'll pull the third trial's numbers now.
options.C: Tonight's good — I'll have all three trials plotted by eight.

question: Which is the most natural reply?

options.B: Sure, I'll sign it and put it through today.
options.C: That signature has to be your instructor's, not mine.
options.D: The late-add form is the yellow one, not the blue.

question: Which is the most natural reply?

options.A: I paid six hundred last month too, same as always.
options.B: Does the six hundred include the ninety for internet?
options.C: Twelve hundred split three ways is four each, not six hundred.
options.D: Sure, I'll transfer my six hundred before the first.
